entries.note: The post is about Amodei's own predictions and says 'a lot of prominent podcasters'. The proposition widens this to 'figures like Amodei' and to podcasters in general. 'Pulled out of hats' is a dismissive figure of speech, not a testable claim about how the dates were set.

entries.test: Amodei's public AGI timeline statements from 2023 to March 2025, checking whether the years he cites moved from 2025-2026 to 2026-2027.
entries.note: The proposition drops Marcus's hedge 'mostly', which makes the claim firmer than he wrote it.

entries.test: Whether any AI system widely accepted as AGI was released or demonstrated in 2025.
entries.note: 'Obviously' marks this as a firm expectation, and the 2025 deadline has passed.
He hedges with 'would likely'. The added 'contrary to claims…' framing is the drafter's, not his words.

entries.test: Documented attempts in early 2025 to have leading AI coding tools build a working Pac-Man clone, and whether they usually succeeded without major fixes.
entries.note: 'Current' refers to tools as of March 2025.

entries.test: Whether nearly all code (in industry generally, or at Anthropic) was written by AI within the roughly 3-12 month window Amodei gave in March 2025.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'seemed … to me' and states the judgment as fact. It is graded here as an implied forecast that Amodei's coding prediction would fail.

entries.test: Archived Anthropic job listings from March 2025, checking the number of openings for software engineers and similar coding roles.
entries.note: Marcus wrote 'allegedly believes'. The proposition instead says Amodei claimed coders are nearly obsolete and adds a firm 'contradicts'.
This is a demand that Anthropic answer questions, not a factual claim.

entries.test: The AAAI 2025 Presidential Panel report on the Future of AI Research, checking the share of respondents who said neural networks alone are insufficient for AGI.
entries.note: The exact percentage should be checked against the published AAAI report.
